buyIn.title: Buy-In & Payouts
items: $125 buy-in x 12 managers = $1,500 total pot
$20 x 14 weeks = $280 (weekly pot, separate from the season-long payout)

keeperRules.title: Keeper Rules
items: Keepers are optional
You can keep up to 2 players, for up to 2 extra seasons each
To keep a player for 1 year — forfeit the draft pick one round earlier than where you drafted them
To keep that same player for another year — forfeit the draft pick two rounds earlier than where you drafted them
Example: keep a 2024 5th-round pick for 1 extra season → forfeit your 2025 4th-round pick
Example: keep that same player again → forfeit your 2026 3rd-round pick the following offseason
Can't keep 1st or 2nd round players
Next year's draft order is always random
To keep a waiver pickup, you give up a round 8 pick — unless they were drafted, in which case their original draft position sets the keeper cost
To keep a player you traded for, you forfeit the pick they were originally drafted at
Playoff teams cannot keep any waiver-wire player claimed after the regular season ends
Consolation bracket teams can only pick up free agents and should not submit waiver claims
If you trade away the pick required to keep a player, you must give up the next best pick instead

keeperSteps.title: How to Select Keepers
keeperSteps.deadlineNote: Deadline: Sunday, August 17th. If your sleeper is injured during the final week of the preseason, you can swap them for another player or decline to claim a sleeper.

tradeRules.title: Trade Rules
items: Any trade involving draft picks must include a pick from the same draft in return — e.g. if you receive a 3rd-round pick, send back at least a 15th-round pick, so every team's roster count stays even
Picks can only be traded up to 2 years in advance (this carries the risk of not knowing the random draft order for that 2nd year)
No veto on preseason trades
Trade deadline is the end of the regular season
Every in-season trade is held to a veto vote
